ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS 
Priceless Treasure found in Geesukonda, Warangal (A.P.) 
*141. SHRI K. KALAVENKATA RAO:  Will the Minister of TOURISM 
AND CULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether priceless treasure has been  found in Geesukonda, Warangal 
(A.P.) in excavation by the archaeologists; 
(b) if so, the details of ancient civilization found; and 
(c) the action taken to preserve the treasure? 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM AND CULTURE (SHRI ANANTH 
KUMAR): (a) and (b) The Department of Archaeology and Museums, Govt, 
of Andhra Pradesh carried out a minor excavation and exploration at 
Geesukonda in district Warangal, AP, in November-December 2000. The 
excavation is reported to have yiel ded archaeological material comprising 
polished stone axes, iron objects, sling balls, foundation of a brick-built 
circular structure, terracotta figurines, beads and bangles, Satavahana and 
Vishnukundi coins. These finds range from Neolithic period to the 4th 
century A.D. 
(c) As per information received from the Government of Andhra Pradesh, 
the excavated material has been chemically cleaned and preserved. 
SHRI K. KALAVENKATA RAO: Sir, my first supplementary is this. 
Geesukonda excavations throw light on the ancient civilisations of 
Satavahana and Vishnu Kund. The archaeologists are, however, 
disappointed, as they could not carry out further investigations, due to 
paucity of funds. I would like to know from the hon. Minister whether   the   
Government   of   India   would   immediately   sanction

Rs. 10 lakhs required to acquire a fou r-acre piece of land which is holding 
the treasure trove of the 1st and 4th Century A.D., for further excavation and 
research. 
SHRI ANANTH KUMAR: Sir, Geesukonda excavations are very 
important excavations. The State Government of Andhra Pradesh has started 
the excavation work two years ago. Us ually, the procedure according to the 
Act, is, the State concerned should seek the permission of the Union 
Government/the Archaeological Survey of India. But, till now, there is no 
application seeking permission for the excavation, from the State 
Government. Sir, the excavation has stopped not because of paucity of funds, 
but because the local pattadars have raised objection. And, secondly, if the 
State Government approaches the Archaeological Survey of India, in a proper 
manner, we will consider the case. 
SHRI K. KALAVENKATA RAO: Sir, my second supplementary is: With 
the onset of monsoon, the treasure might get affected, as the owner of the land 
is tilling it for agricultural produce. So, the Government take steps to declare 
the area as a "protected area" and take action to excavate the treasure fully, at 
an early date, with the assistance of the Government of Andhra Pradesh? 
SHRI ANANTH KUMAR: Sir, we w ill have correspondence with the 
State Government regarding this because, the State Government, suo moto, 
without even informing the Union Government and the Archaeological 
Survey of India, has started the excava tion there. It is the first of its kind 
which has happened. Actually, there is the Central Advisory Board on 
Archaeology which has a Standing Committee, and whatever excavations are 
proposed to be conducted, the proposal has to go to that Standing Committee 
and the Standing Committee would make a list and propose the same to the 
DGASI, and the DGASI will take up the excavations, centrally. This is the 
procedure. Now, this procedure has no t been followed in this case. They 
started the excavation work in November/December, 2000, and it has come to 
our notice, through an Unstarred Question, in 2001. Therefore, if there is an 
application, in the due format, to the Union Government, we will take up the 
matter.

Deployment of Special Service Battalion along Indo-Nepal Border 
*148. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR : Will the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has decided to deploy a Special Service Battalion 
of a Special Police Organisation along Indo-Nepal border in Bihar to control 
trans-border activities, including smuggling and I.S.I, activities; 
(b) whether this has been done after some anti-national activities came to 
Government's notice; and 
(c) if so, the details of such activities? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI I.D. SWAMI): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) and (c) Of late, Indo-Nepal border has emerged as a vital link in 
Pakistans prolonged low intensity proxy war against India. Pak ISI  has been 
misusing this open border for launching major terrorist offensives against 
India. Militants from Kashmir and Punjab also continue to take shelter in 
Nepal and there is a growing nexus between militants/anti-India elements 
based in Nepalese territory with their counterparts on the Indian side of the 
border. This is in addition to other trans-border criminal activities like 
smuggling of contraband, explosives and fake Indian currency for which this 
border has been used for quite some time. 
37 

RAJYA SABHA [1st August 2001] 
Laying of roads and development of watersheds in villages 
*149. SHRI YADLAPATI VENKAT RAO: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether schemes relating to laying of roads and development of 
watersheds in villages are decided by Union Government; and 
(b) if so, the reasons for not consulting the State Governments to accord 
priority in their development? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI M. VENKAIAH 
NAIDU): (a) and (b) The Rural Roads projects under the Pradhan Mantri 
Gram Sadak Yojana are formulated by the State Governments, keeping in 
view the Guidelines issued under the Programme. The projects are executed 
by the State authorities, after clearance of the same in the Government of 
India. 
Projects relating to Watersheds are covered under three Programmes viz. 
the Integrated Wastelands Development Programme (IWDP), the Drought 
Prone Areas Programme (DPAP) and the Desert Development Programme 
(DDP). Under the IWDP, the projects are sanctioned by the Department of 
Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Deve lopment, after their prioritization in 
consultation with the concerned State Governments. As regards the DPAP 
and the DDP, the Government of India decide the number of new projects to 
be sanctioned to a Programme District, keeping in view the Annual Budget 
Allocation as well as the performance of the District in the execution of 
ongoing Watershed Projects. The exact location of the projects is determined 
by the concerned DRDAs/Zilla Panchayats, in consultation with the State 
Governments.

Need for Global look for Indian Textile Industry 
*152. SHRI RUMANDLA RAMACHANDRAIAH: Will the Minister of 
TEXTILES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government have deci ded to face the challenges of the 
rapidly changing world textiles scenario by stressing the need for Indian 
Textile Industry to consider itself as operating in a global market; 
(b) if so, to what extent, the textile industry has changed its course for 
operating in a global market; and 
(c) the steps taken by Government in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI KASHIRAM RANA): (a) to (c) 
The Government is fully committed to face the challanges of globalisation by 
encouraging investments for modernisation and upgradation of the textile 
industry. 
The National Textile Policy-2000 (NTxP-2000), provides an enabling 
environment to make the domestic text ile industry strong enough to face 
growing global competition. De-reservation of the woven segment of 
readymade garment sector will allow the industry to achieve desired 
economies of scale. In order to implement the vision of the NTxP-2000, a 
"Textile Package" was announced in the Budget 2001-02 to encourage 
investment in the textile sector. Some of the important provisions of the 
"Textile Package" are:—  
(i) Customs duty has been reduced from 15% to 5% on 159 specified 
textile and garment machineries. In addition, 12 important items of 
machineries including shuttleless looms have also been exempted 
from additional excise duty. 
40 

[1st August 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
A programme has been announced to induct 50,000 shuttleless 
looms and to modernise 2.5 lakh powerlooms in the decentralised 
sector by 2004. 
(ii) Assistance under Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS) 
providing for a reimbursement of 5% out of interest, is available 
to the textile industry for modernisation and upgradation. In 
addition, rate of depreciation allowance for machinery under 
TUFS has been raised to 50%. 
(iii) A provision of Rs. 10 cror es has been earmarked in the B udget 
2001-02 for the establishment of Apparel Parks for production 
and export of garments. Besides a provision of Rs. 15 crores has 
been made for the Scheme for improvement of critical 
infrastructure facilities at major textile production centres. 
In addition, a Technology Mission on Cotton (TMC) with an outlay of 
about Rs. 600 crores has been launched by the Government to improve the 
productivity and quality of cotton required by the textile industry.

(GoM) under the Chairmanship of Finance Minister has also been functioning 
to reveiw and monitor the drought mitigation efforts.

renovation,  restoratior

* If captive plant is of Hydro or Cogeneration, such plant, irrespective of

proposal for installation of the captive power plant can be considered. 
* If the cost of generation from captive power plant is found to be lower, 
the proposal may be considered after examining the cost and tariff. 
* Units in Special Economic Zone (SEZs) and/industrial entities may be 
allowed to set up captive power plants liberally. 
* Banking facilities are proposed to be provided to CPPs. The rates for

Electrification of villages in Arunachal Pradesh 
1149. SHRI NABAM REBIA: Will the Mi nister of POWER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether Central Government have formulated any concrete scheme 
for electrification of the villages in the State of Arunachal Pradesh; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of villages in the State that have been electrified, so 
far; and 
(d) by when, all the villages of State are likely to be electrified? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER 
(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) to (d) Rural Electrification has 
now been included under Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana (PMGY). 
Finance Minister in his Speech while presenting the Union Budget for 
2001-2002 has announced that a package of initiatives is being launched by 
the Government to improve the power distribution system in rural areas. This 
includes: 
120 

[1st August 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
(i)  Completion  of electrification  of bulk  of the   remaining villages 
in the next six years. 
(ii) Extension of assistance to the States for village electrification works 
under the Prime Minister's Gramodaya Yojana (PMGY) whose 
funding is being augmented. 
(iii) Stepping up credit support from  Rural Electrification Corporation 
to SEBs for speedy electrification of dalit bastis; households of 
scheduled tribes and other weaker sections of society; 
(iv) Improving the quality of power supply in villages. 
(v) Augmentation of distribution networks in rural areas supported by 
REC under the Accelerated Power Development Programme 
(APDP). 
(vi) Earmarking a sum of Rs. 750 crores out of RIDF by allowing it to 
float capital gains tax exemption bonds along with NABARD and 
NHAl under Section 54 EC of the Income Tax Act. 
The un-electrified villages in the State of Arunachal Pradesh would get 
covered accordingly. As per CEA's sta tistics, out of total 3649 inhabited 
villages (1991 census), 2206 villages have been reported to be electrified as 
on 31st March, 2001. In addition, a scheme for electrification of 60 villages at 
a cost of Rs. 897 lakhs has also been approved for implementation out of Non-
Lapsable Central Pool of Resources. 
Government have set the goal of 100% electrification of villages feasible to 
be connected with the Grid by 2007. Th e remote villages are proposed to be 
electrified using non-conventional sources of energy by the year 2012.

(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) Yes, Sir.

the Dabhol Power Project on 15th September, 1994. The Dabhol Power 
Project was re-negotiated by the Government of Maharashtra (GOM) during 
1995-96. The terms and conditions of the counter guarantee require that any 
amendment to the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) would require the prior 
written consent 
125 

RAJYA SABHA [1st August 2001] 
of GOI. Since the re-negotiated features of the project called for an amendment

the new Government on 9.7.1996, which approved extension of GOI counter 
guarantee to the re-negotiated project without any changes in terms and conditions 
of the GOI counter guarantee.

Dabhol Power Company (DPC) on the one hand and the Maharashtra State 
Electricity Board (MSEB)/GOM on the other in regard to obligations of 
respective parties arising out of the PPA and the guarantee issued by the GOM to

notices to GOM and MSEB as well as two pre-termination notices to MSEB. 
MSEB have written to DPC on 23.5. 2001 rescinding the PPA due to alleged 
misrepresentations by DPC in respect of capacity and capability of the Dabhol 
Power Station. Conciliation proceedings between the Government of India 
(GOI) and DPC in regard to obligations under the counter guarantee issued to 
the project by GOI, have also been initiated by DPC. Meanwhile, a 
Negotiating Committee has also been set up by the Government of 
Maharashtra to carry out discussions with DPC with a view to reducing the tariff 
as well as sale of power of the Dabhol Power Project. The GOI has appointed its 
nominee on the Negotiating Committee and is committed to help facilitate an 
amicable solution to the problems.

Electrification of villages through renewable energy sources 
1156. SHRI S. RAMACHANDRAN PILLAI: Will the Minister of 
POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have fixed a goal of generating 10 per cent share 
in the additional power generation by the year 2012 which would work out to 
10,000 MW; 
(b) whether Government have also devised an action plan to electrify 
80,000 villages over the next seven years through renewable energy sources; 
and 
(c) if so, what steps are being taken to achieve both the targets? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER 
(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) to (c) Based on the findings of the 
16th Electric Power Survey, it has been estimated that an additional capacity 
of 1,07,000 MW is required to be added by 2012 to meet the energy 
requirement of 975 BUs. The Ministry of Non-Conventional Energy Sources 
have prepared a Draft Renewable Energy Policy Statement which envisages 
10% or 10,000 MW of the add itional planned capacity to come from non-
conventional energy sources by the year 2012. 
There are about 79,000 villages as on 1.4.2001 which remain to be electrified 
in the country. Out of this, about 18,000 villages are in remote and in 
difficult areas. The Ministry of Non-Conventional Energy Sources proposes 
to implement a programme for electrification of villages in remote and 
difficult areas in the country 
136 

[1st August 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
during the next 10-11 years. Consultations have been held with State 
Governments, NGOs, financial institutions and manufacturers to develop an 
action plan for this purpose. State Governments have been asked to send lists 
of un-electrified villages which cannot be electrified by conventional means. 
A provision of Rs. 20 crores has been included in the budget of the Ministry 
for 2001-02 to initiate implementation of this programme.

pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Nort h Eastern Electric Power Corporation 
(NEEPCO) is running with an ad-hoc CMD; 
(b) whether key posts in the Board- of  Directors are lying vacant with 
many of the Directors due to retire soon; 
(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(d) the action taken to fill up these key posts for better functioning of 
NEEPCO in the light of news-item in Assam Tribune dated 8th July, 2001 
captioned "Outstanding dues posing problems for NEEPCO"? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER 
(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) to (d) The posts of Chairman & 
Managing Director and Director (Finance), North Eastern Electric Power 
Corporation (NEEPCO) fell vacant with effect from 1.11.2000 and 1.3.2001 
respectively consequent upon the retir ement of respective incumbents. The 
delay in the filling up these posts wa s on account of consultation process 
related certain administrative procedures and late receipt of requisite 
information and documents from the respective organizations where the 
selected candidates arc employed. Thes e cases have since been processed 
and on receipt of the approval of the Competent Authority, the posts of CMD 
Director (F), NEEPCO would be filled.

One-time settlement formula for SEBs outstanding dues 
1158. SHRI SOLIPETA RAMACHANDRA REDDY: 
 SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY:  
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether some States have approached the Union Government to provide 
more time to study the proposed one-time settlement formula for the State 
Electricity Boards outstanding dues; 
(b) if so, the States that have made such a request and the total amount of 
dues, State-wise; 
(c) the details of the penalties imposed by the Union Government and the. 
reaction of the State Governments; and 
(d) what final decision has been taken by Union Government for the 
settlement of the dues? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHRIMATI 
JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) and (b) Recently Minister of Power has written to 
Chief Ministers of States and UTs urging them to initiate steps for 
implementation of the one time Scheme of settlement of outstanding dues of State 
Electricity Boards. Response to Minister of Power's letter is awaited. Statement 
of outstanding dues payable to CPSUs of Ministry of Power as on 30.4.2001 is 
given in the Statement (See below). 
(c) and (d) The scheme proposed by the Expert Group on one time settlement of 
dues of SEBs has many incentives and some penalties. The details of the scheme 
recommended by the Expert Group are as under: 
(a) The Group recommended 50 per cent waiver of surcharge/  
interest on delayed payments. 
(b) For the remaining dues i.e. the entire principal outstanding as well as the 
remaining 50% surcharge, bonds would be issued by the respective 
State Governments. 
(c) The bonds would be issued through RBI at a tax free interest rate of 
8.5% p.a. 
138 

[1st August 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
(d) The bonds should be structured to achieve a moratorium of 5 years on 
repayment of principal with the entire principal being repaid between 
the 6th and 15th year. 
(c) These bonds shall be identical to bonds issued in connection with the 
market borrowings of State Governments, with the attendant discipline in 
repayments. The bonds will be subject to lock-in restrictions that will 
allow release of only 10 per cent of the bonds in the secondary market 
each year. 
(f) For ensuring timely payment of current dues in future, defaults in 
current payment for power/fuel should attract a graded reduction in the 
supply of power from central power stations and in coal supplies. Where 
such defaults exceed 90 days from the date of b illing, the Ministry of 
Finance should recover these dues through adjustment against releases 
dues to them from the Centre. 
(g) As part of the scheme, SEBs should accept reform-based performance 
milestones such as setting up SERCs, metering of distribution feeders 
and improvement in revenue realisation. The milestones should be 
specified in the MOUs to be signed with the Ministry of Power. 
(h) The States should be offered incentives for complying with the 
scheme. If SEBs do not default on their current dues and adhere to the 
performance milestones, CPSUs should pay them, during the first 
four years commencing from 1.4.2001, bi-annual cash incentives 
equal to 2 per cent of the value of bonds. 
(i) Further, if SEBs open and maintain LCs till the end of December, 2001, 
CPSUs should pay them a one-time cash incentive equal to 2 per cent 
of the value of bonds. 
(j) In addition, States undertaking reforms should also be assisted thro ugh 
APDP grants and discretionary allocation of power. 
(k) This scheme should enter into force only after one-half of 
139 

RAJYA SABHA [1st August 2001] 
the States that have an annual billing of over Rs. 500 crore per annum 
from CPSUs give their consent, and should be effective in respect of 
the States that give such consent. 
(1) The States that withhold their consent beyond 60 days after this 
scheme enters into force should be denied any share in the 
discretionary allocation of 15 per cent from the power stations of 
CPSUs as well as any assistance unde r APDP. If the ovcrducs of such 
States exceeded Rs. 50 crores in respect of any CPSU, they should also 
attract reduction in power and coal supplies, as applicable to the States 
participating in this scheme. 
Following the submission of the Report of the Expert Group a high level 
Empowered Group consisting of Finance Minister, Dy. Chairman, Planning 
Commission, Minister of Power and Chief Ministers of some States met on 
26.6.2001 and 6.7.2001. The Empowered Group endorsed the 
recommendations of the Expert Group with the following modifications: 
(i) Waiver of surcharge would now be 60% instead of 50%  as 
recommended by the Group. 
(ii) The incentives for achieving th e reform-based milestones shall be 
increased to 6% in the first year and 5% in the second year.

Arsenic poisoning of ground water in West Bengal 
1166. SHRI NILOTPAL BASU: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have decided to stop funding 
under the special Centrally sponsored scheme in West Bengal 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
158 

[1st August 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
for tackling the problem of arsenic poisoning of the ground water in vast 
stretches of the State; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; and 
(c) whether this is to imply that the dimension of the problem has been 
reduced substantially, so much so, that it does not further warrant any 
Central support? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT [DR. (SHRIMATI) RITA VERMA]: (a) No, Sir. 
(b) and (c) Rural drinking water supply is a State subject. State 
Governments take up schemes/projects for providing drinking water in rural 
areas from their own resources. Government of India supplements the efforts 
of the State Governments and provide financial assistance under Accelerated 
Rural Water Supply Programme (ARWSP) and Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya 
Yojana (PMGY)— Rural Drinking Water (RDW). Under ARWSP, up to 
20% of the allotted funds can be utilised to tackle water quality problem 
which inter-alia includes providing safe drinking water free from arsenic 
contamination and sustainability of sources. As reported by the Government 
of West Bengal, as on 1.4.1999, out of  total 79,036 rural habitations in the 
State 3,133 habitations are affected with arsenic contamination. 
To tackle arsenic contamination in drinking water, prior to 1.4.1998, under 
Sub-Mission programme of ARWSP, 3 projects were sanctioned to West 
Bengal at a total approved cost of Rs. 259.79 crore, out of which 
Government of India's share is about Rs. 194.84 crore and State share is Rs. 
64.95 crore. So far Government of India has released Rs. 180.13 crore. 
Remaining funds Rs. 14.71 crore will be released on the basis of the progress 
of implementation and fulfillment of conditions laid down for the released of 
funds. Since 
159

1.4.1998, powers to plan, approve and implement schemes under Sub-
Mission have been delegated to the States. States can also take up 
schemes/projects to provide safe drinking water under PMGY-RDW and 
powers to approve schemes/projects have been delegated to State 
Governments. During 2000-2001, Rs. 78.37 crore under ARWSP and Rs. 
58.74 crore under RDW component of PMGY were released. For the current 
year, Rs. 43.86 crore under ARWSP and Rs. 9.40 crore under RDW 
component of PMGY have been released as 1st installment. 
Keeping in view the problem of arsenic contamination in ground water in 
the State, as a special case, instead of 20%, 50% of ARWSP funds have been 
allowed to be spent on tackling arsenic contamination in 24 North Parganas 
District. As per information received from the Government of West Bengal, 
after 1.4.1998, during 2000-2001, State Government has sanctioned two 
projects—one project in Nort h 24 Parganas District at a total cost of Rs. 
124.82 crore covering 318 habitations under ARWSP and another project in 
Malda district at a total cost of Rs . 43.00 crore covering 367 habitations 
under PMGY—Rural Drinking Water, for tackling arsenic problem in 
drinking watet.

160 
 

[1st August 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI M. VENKAIAH 
NAIDU): (a) Yes, Sir. A Conference of  State Ministers of Panchayati Raj 
was held on 11.07.2001 at New Delhi. 
(b) The subjects discussed and broad consensus arrived at in the 
conference are given in the Statement (See below) 
Statement 
Major recommendations of the Conference of State Ministers of 
Panchayati Raj held on 11.07.2001 at New Delhi 
The following resolutions/recommendations on strengthening of 
Panchayati Raj Institutions were adopted unanimously by the State Ministers 
of Panchayati Raj present in the Conference. 
(i) Elections—  
 It was agreed that since the holding of Panchayat elections every 5 years 
is mandatory, State Governments/Union Territory Administration shall 
ensure that elections are held with the same regularity with which 
Parliament and Assembly elections are held. 
 States/UTs should refrain from  approaching Law Courts for 
postponement of elections. While the adequacy of the legal provisions 
pertaining to Panchayat elections  can be examined, the State 
Governments have to, in the first instance, ensure regular holding of 
elections. 
 It was desirable of Panchayat elections to be held on non-party basis. 
 The process of delimitation of constituencies and reservation of seats for 
SCs/STs and women should be settled well in advance, for giving 
sufficient opportunity for settling disputes, if any, on these issues. 
 If Panchayat elections are not held on time, the Planning 
Commission/Government of India can issue directions for withholding 
funds under Central Schemes/Centrally Sponsored Schemes. 
161 

RAJYA SABHA [1st August 2001] 
(ii) Devolution of funds, functions and functionaries upon PRIs—  
 It was agreed that States/UTs would devolve functions upon PRIs in 
respect of the subjects listed in the XI schedule and issue detailed 
executive instructions devolving specific and substantial executive 
powers upon each tier of' Panchayats by 31.3.2002. 
 A Task Force comprising senior officers of the Ministry of Rural 
Development and of the State Governments will be set up at the earliest 
to operationalise administrative decentralization of funds, functions 
and functionaries with regard to the subjects in the Constitution, so 
that functional and financial devolution is completed by 31st March, 
2002. 
 Incentives should be extended to the Panchayats by the State 
Governments by way of grants-in-aids for their better performance as 
regards raising their own resources. 
 Panchayats may be given untied funds to enable them to select 
development work according to their needs. 
(iii) Constitution of DPCs—  
 The Conference, taking note of the poor progress in setting up of 
District Planning Committees in  most of the States/UTs, 
recommended that these be constituted by the end of 2001. 
 It was agreed that the practice of  appointing Minister-in-charge of 
district as Chairperson of DPC should be discontinued and that the 
Chairman of District Panchayat o ught to be the Chairperson of the 
DPC. 
(iv) Strengthening of Gram Sabha—  
 In order to accelerate the emergence of Gram Sabhas as bodies to 
whom the PRIs are accountable, the powers and functions of Gram 
Sabha should be spelt out in detail articulating their role as planners, 
decision-makers,and auditors. 
 It was agreed that the Gram Sabha meeting should be held at least 
four times in a year. Instead of holding the Gram Sabha on a fixed 
day, it was suggested to hold Gram Sabhas within a span of 30 days 
from the pre-detcrmined dates so that concerned officers are present 
to respond to questions and concerns. 
162 

[1st August 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
(v) Transparency and Accountability—  
 It was resolved that the following 4-point strategy for strengthening of Gram  
Sabha and effective  implementation of different  Rural Development 
Schemes will be implemented in letter and spirit:—  
 Awareness through print and electronic media, street plays and training to 
the elected Panchayat representatives; 
 Participation of the community in th e preparation of need based action 
plans, their execution and monitoring; 
 Transparency by displaying all the relevant information on a Bill Board 
regarding estimates, availability of funds and expenditure on the works 
taken, up by the Panchayats, making available all relevant records for 
inspection by the public, providing photocopies of documents, on demand 
on payment of nominal charges and prescribing well-defined methods for 
selection of beneficiaries; 
 Social Audit should have binding legal outcomes so as to curb corruption 
and misutilisation of funds. The Gram Sabha should be empowered 
legally for Social Audit. 
(vi) State Control over PRIs—  
 The scope of State Government intervention and control over 
PRIs should be minimized. If there is any specific complaint 
against any Panchayat, it should be referred to a body similar 
to the Ombudsman in Kerala. 
(vii) Parallel Bodies constituted by States—  
 The Conference decried the increas ing tendency to set up parallel 
bodies. If at all any such bodies arc to be set up, they should work 
under the supervision of the Panchayats and the Gram Sabha. 
 The Conference recommended that instead of setting up parallel 
bodies, States should implement the existing provision in Panchayat 
laws for Sub-Committees on different subjects and train Panchayat 
Members for this purpose. 
 Panchayats/Gram Sabhas should be empowered to supervise and 
monitor the work of NGOs working in the rural areas. 
163 

RAJYA SABHA [1st August 2001] 
(viii) The Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled 
Areas) Act 1996-[PESA—1996 ] 
 It was agreed that action would be taken to ensure legislation or 
amendment of relevant Acts/Rules, to bring them in conformity with 
the provisions of the PESA, 1996, latest by 31.3.2002.

of important craft clusters and their sustainable development; revival of

introduction of Baba Saheb Ambedkar Hastshilp Vikas Yojna; development &

Mr. Chairman, Sir, yesterday, when I began my reply to the debate in 
this House, I was trying to put thin gs in perspective. What is the 
challenge before us, today? Sir, the challenge is to restore the 
confidence of the investors in UTl generally, and in US-64, in 
particular. It is to restore the count ry's confidence in the financial 
sector of this country. Sir, the finan cial sector of this country does not 
belong to this Government or that Government, or, this party or that 
party. The financial sector of the co untry belongs to the entire nation. 
The financial sector of the country not only deals with matters within 
the country, it also interacts with international agencies, international 
banks, international parties, and, therefore, it is of the utmost 
importance that that confidence in th e financial market is not only fully 
restored, but that we create a sit uation where that confidence is not 
tested again, that confidence is  not endangered again. That I 
presume, that I suppose, is the challenge that we face as Government, 
as Parliament, and as a nation. It is in that context, Sir, - because we 
have to look to the future - in order to be able to look to the future, it is 
important for us to look back a little and find out what exactly 
happened. And it was not with the intention of apportioning blame to 
this Government or that Government, but with a view to understanding 
the nature of the problem, Sir, I was trying to put before this hon. 
House certain facts on this issue, and I started by saying that there 
was a time when the nature of this fund underwent a change. I 
referred to certain facts, how the 28 per cent equity became almost 70 
per cent equity, as far as US-64 was concerned; and how the fund 
became subject to fluctuations in the stock market. I was also. Sir, 
mentioning that the fund gave ve ry high dividends during a certain 
period. Now, these high dividends would have been entirely justified, if 
they had been paid out of the earn ings. But, unfortunately, according 
to the figures which have been made available to me by the UTl, I find 
that at least during 3 years, nam ely, 1994-95. 1995-96 and 1996-97, 
the UTl drew upon reserves, and to what extent? Rs. 684 crores in 
1994-95; Rs. 1147 crores in 1995-96; and Rs. 390 crores in 1996-97. 
These were the drawals from the rese rves of the UTl in order to pay 
these high dividends.    Nobody was

this category of non-individuals? The entities are public sector banks.

that day also I was trying to make this point in the House -- that 
nobody has run away with this money. A large portion of the money 
withdrawn from the UTI has gone to individuals, even in the month of 
May. As much as Rs.811 crores has gone to public sector banks. The 
amount withdrawn by the private se ctor banks is Rs. 149.73 crores.

out of a total redemption of Rs.3,682 crores in the month of May, the 
withdrawal by corporates is Rs. 1.033 crores.
